group.title: Academic basics
sources: Word choice guided by general-purpose and academic frequency ideas (NGSL and AWL families); all meanings and sentences are original.

words.meaning: To study something carefully to understand it.
examples: Scientists {analyze} the data from the experiment.
wrong: I analyze the report without reading it.
She analyzed to the data.

words.meaning: To give reasons to show that something is true or false.
examples: Some people {argue} that homework is helpful.
wrong: He argues the table with milk.
I argued of the idea.

words.meaning: To think that something is true without checking.
examples: Don't {assume} that everyone has a phone.
wrong: I assumed the answer after I checked every fact twice.
She assumes to know it.

words.meaning: A good result or advantage.
examples: One {benefit} of exercise is better sleep.
wrong: One benefit of the storm is that it destroyed our roof.
He benefits of a lot.

words.meaning: An idea about how something works or what it means.
examples: The {concept} of time is hard to explain.
wrong: My concept is a warm sandwich.
She concepts the lesson.

words.meaning: A result of an action or event.
examples: Missing the deadline had serious {consequences}.
wrong: The consequence came before the action.
He consequences of the choice.

words.meaning: A clear difference between two things.
examples: There is a sharp {contrast} between the two cities.
wrong: There is a big contrast because the two cities are exactly the same.
She contrast two ideas.

words.meaning: To say exactly what a word or idea means.
examples: The teacher asked us to {define} the term.
wrong: I define the table to the moon.
She defined to the word.

words.meaning: Facts or signs that show something is true.
examples: The police found new {evidence}.
wrong: He has no evidence, but he is completely sure it is a fact.
The evidences are on the desk.

words.meaning: One of the things that affect a result.
examples: Cost is an important {factor} in the decision.
wrong: A factor is a result that has no cause.
She factors the decision.

words.meaning: The purpose or normal job of something.
examples: The {function} of the heart is to pump blood.
wrong: The function of a key is to cut bread.
He functions of the machine.

words.meaning: A strong effect on something.
examples: The new law had a big {impact} on small shops.
wrong: The law had a big impact, but nothing changed.
She impacts of the law.

words.meaning: To show or point to something.
examples: The results {indicate} that the plan works.
wrong: The results indicate that nobody knows anything.
He indicated to the sign.

words.meaning: One single person, not a group.
examples: Each {individual} has different needs.
wrong: An individual is a big group of people.
She individual of the group.

words.meaning: To explain what something means.
examples: People can {interpret} the poem in different ways.
wrong: I interpret the poem by not reading it.
He interpreted of the sign.

words.meaning: A problem or topic that people discuss.
examples: Climate change is an important {issue}.
wrong: An issue is something no one talks about or thinks about.
She issues of the city.

words.meaning: A particular way of doing something.
examples: This {method} saves a lot of time.
wrong: The method is the final answer of the test.
He methods the research.

words.meaning: To get something, often with effort.
examples: You can {obtain} a permit at the town hall.
wrong: I obtained a permit by giving it away.
She obtains from a license.

words.meaning: To happen.
examples: The accident did not {occur} at night.
wrong: The event occurred, but nothing happened.
He occurs to the street.

words.meaning: A basic rule or idea that guides how you act or think.
examples: Honesty is a basic {principle} in science.
wrong: A principle is the person who runs a school.
She principles of the club.

words.meaning: A series of steps that lead to a result.
examples: Making cheese is a long {process}.
wrong: The process has no steps and no end.
He process the milk for cheese.

words.meaning: To need something or make it necessary.
examples: The job will {require} two years of experience.
wrong: The job requires nothing, so you must bring many documents.
She requires to have a license.

words.meaning: Careful study to find new facts.
examples: Her {research} shows how children learn.
wrong: I did research by guessing without looking at any facts.
He researches are on the shelf.

words.meaning: To answer or react to something.
examples: Please {respond} to the email by Friday.
wrong: I responded before I read the email.
She responds the letter.

words.meaning: The part someone or something plays in a situation.
examples: Parents play an important {role} in learning.
wrong: A role is a kind of bread.
He roles in the project.

words.meaning: Important enough to have a clear effect.
examples: There was a {significant} change in the numbers.
wrong: The change was significant because it was too small to notice.
She significants a result.

words.meaning: A place, person or thing where information or something else comes from.
examples: The report names its {source} for each fact.
wrong: The report has no source and no one wrote it.
He sources of the river.

words.meaning: The way parts are arranged to make a whole.
examples: The {structure} of the essay is clear.
wrong: The essay has no structure, so every part is in perfect order.
She structure the paragraph.

words.meaning: A set of questions asked to many people to learn their opinions.
examples: The {survey} asked students about their sleep.
wrong: The survey asked only one person and no questions.
He surveys of the class.

words.meaning: An idea that tries to explain how or why something happens.
examples: Darwin's {theory} explains how species change.
wrong: A theory is a fact that nobody can explain.
She theory the results.

words.meaning: A general change or direction over time.
examples: There is a growing {trend} toward working from home.
wrong: A trend is something that happens only once.
He trends of the market.

words.meaning: A number of different kinds of things.
examples: The store sells a wide {variety} of teas.
wrong: The store has a wide variety, so every product is the same.
She varieties of cakes.

words.meaning: A form of something that is a little different from others.
examples: This is the newest {version} of the app.
wrong: This version is exactly the same as every other one.
He versions the app.

words.meaning: To look at things to see how they are alike or different.
examples: Let's {compare} the two phones before we buy one.
wrong: I compare one phone without looking at the other.
She compares at the prices.

words.meaning: To decide something after thinking about the facts.
examples: We {conclude} that the plan is safe.
wrong: I concluded the answer before I knew any facts.
He concludes to the idea.

words.meaning: To make something new.
examples: Artists {create} new things every day.
wrong: I created a painting that already existed.
She creates of a song.

words.meaning: To guess an amount using the facts you have.
examples: Can you {estimate} how long the trip will take?
wrong: I estimate the exact number after I measure it.
He estimates to the cost.

words.meaning: To give all your attention to one thing.
examples: I cannot {focus} when the room is noisy.
wrong: I focus on ten different things at the same time.
She focuses at the work.

words.meaning: To include someone or something as a necessary part.
examples: The job will {involve} a lot of travel.
wrong: The plan involves nobody and nothing.
He involves to the group.

words.meaning: To keep something in good condition or at the same level.
examples: It is hard to {maintain} a healthy diet when you travel.
wrong: We maintain the road by letting it break.
She maintains of the house.
